ENGLISH LANGUAGE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #11
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What is turn-taking in a conversation? (1 mark)
   A. One person speaks all the time
   B. Both people speak at the same time
   C. One person speaks while the other listens, then they swap
   D. Only the teacher speaks

2. Poems and similes: Which is a simile? (1 mark)
   A. She is a bird.
   B. She sang like a bird.
   C. She sang loudly.
   D. She sang.

3. Which simile compares using 'as ... as'? (1 mark)
   A. The maize grew tall.
   B. The tall maize stood.
   C. The maize was as tall as a door.
   D. The maize like a door.

4. Which word has the long vowel /iː/? (1 mark)
   A. sit
   B. bit
   C. ship
   D. sheep

5. Why is it good to read a newspaper regularly? (1 mark)
   A. It cannot teach anything
   B. It gives you money
   C. It replaces school
   D. You learn what is happening and new words

6. Choose the correct -ing form of 'lie' (to rest flat). (1 mark)
   A. lieing
   B. lying
   C. lyeing
   D. liing

7. In 'The Clean-Up Day', which proverb did Kamau use about fixing the hole in the fence? (1 mark)
   A. A stitch in time saves nine
   B. Prevention is better than cure
   C. Look before you leap
   D. Many hands make light work

8. Which word is an adverb of place? (1 mark)
   A. soon
   B. always
   C. outside
   D. gently

9. Which word begins with a silent h? (1 mark)
   A. honest
   B. help
   C. house
   D. hand

10. Pronouns: Which is correct? (1 mark)
   A. Ali and I went to the clinic.
   B. Ali and me went to the clinic.
   C. Ali and myself went to the clinic.
   D. Me and Ali went to the clinic.

11. What is a virus? (1 mark)
   A. A tiny germ that can make people ill
   B. A type of food
   C. A kind of medicine
   D. A sharp tool

12. In the passage about netball, how many players are in a team? (1 mark)
   A. five
   B. seven
   C. nine
   D. eleven

13. What should you do before writing a narrative? (1 mark)
   A. Skip the beginning
   B. Make a short plan
   C. Write the ending only
   D. Copy someone else's story

14. The verb 'record' (to make a record) is stressed on (1 mark)
   A. the first syllable
   B. neither
   C. the second syllable
   D. both

15. Complete: 'This bag is mine and that bag is ___.' (belonging to you) (1 mark)
   A. you
   B. yours
   C. your
   D. yourself

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. Write a short talk of four sentences on how to care for a sick friend. (4 marks)

17. Describe three things you do before, while and after reading a story. (3 marks)

18. Use when, where, who and whose in four questions about a sports day. (4 marks)

19. Write two minimal pairs for /p/ and /b/. (2 marks)

20. Give two reasons why we plan before writing a story. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #11 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — One person speaks while the other listens, then they swap
   In turn-taking each speaker waits for the other to finish before speaking.

2. B — She sang like a bird.
   Like a bird compares her singing to a bird's.

3. C — The maize was as tall as a door.
   'As tall as a door' is an as ... as simile.

4. D — sheep
   'Sheep' has a long /iː/; the others have a short /ɪ/.

5. D — You learn what is happening and new words
   Regular reading builds knowledge and vocabulary.

6. B — lying
   The letters ie change to y before -ing.

7. A — A stitch in time saves nine
   He wanted to fix the small hole before it got worse.

8. C — outside
   'Outside' tells where.

9. A — honest
   'Honest' is said 'onest'.

10. A — Ali and I went to the clinic.
   I is the subject form.

11. A — A tiny germ that can make people ill
   A virus is a tiny germ.

12. B — seven
   The passage says two teams of seven players.

13. B — Make a short plan
   A plan helps organise beginning, middle and end.

14. C — the second syllable
   The verb is re-CORD.

15. B — yours
   Yours is the possessive pronoun for you.

SECTION B
----
16. (4 marks)
   Answer: A greeting, two caring actions such as visiting and listening, and a closing thank-you.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of the four parts.

17. (3 marks)
   Answer: Before: read the title and predict. While: read slowly and find meanings of new words. After: answer questions and retell.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each stage.

18. (4 marks)
   Answer: For example: When is sports day? Where is it held? Who is the guest of honour? Whose team is winning?
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct question.

19. (2 marks)
   Answer: For example: pin, bin and pat, bat.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

20. (2 marks)
   Answer: It puts ideas in order and makes sure we do not forget important events.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.
